title: RWB-S9-AD022-APP: the partner user catalogue, the date trigger, the recall event and the legacy predecessor are unstated
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md (RWB-AD-022); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S9 Partner management v2.md
section: s3 Preconditions, s4 Flow, s9 State transitions, s11 Data, s12.3 Events published, s12.6 Schedules, s18 Traceability
description: Combined for this story: (a) partner_user is a table of S9 in the ownership rows but has no entry in the TSD S9 T3.1 field catalogue, no screen column and no element, so its fields are taken from the Logical Data Model rows DF-REF-212 to DF-REF-217 (identity_ref, partner_id, role_code, valid_from, valid_to); (b) AC2 says 'when the day ends' while FSD S9 A2.12.4.4 declares no background event for the feature and no source names a trigger, a Schedule or a clock time for the pass, and DP-10 and RWB-PLT-E1071-CON are not in the pattern or build rows; (c) no source names an event that announces a recall or an account ending, and the service's event pair is EV-20 InstructionIssued and EV-21 PartnerResultSubmitted; (d) the legacy dependency RWB-E1-022 has no content in any extract and the plan's H row carries the CON and the edge contract instead; (e) TSD S9 T8 maps REQ-S9-005, REQ-S9-006 and REQ-S9-007 to FEAT-PRM-08 while FSD S9 A2.12 publishes the contract end as FEAT-PRM-12.
evidence: TSD S9 T3.1 lists partner and partner_instruction only; TSD S9 T3.2 has no account list; FSD S9 A2.12.4.4 'No background event'; context pack ownership rows give Jobs: None and the events EV-20 and EV-21; legacy RWB-AD-022 metadata row 'Depends on RWB-E1-022'; TSD S9 T8 rows REQ-S9-001 to REQ-S9-009 against FEAT-PRM-01 and FEAT-PRM-08.
proposed: Publish the partner_user fields in the TSD S9 T3.1 catalogue and the PRD, name the contract-end Schedule and its clock, decide whether a recall is announced by an event, and confirm the feature the requirement rows serve.

title: RWB-S9-AD022-CON: no element for the partner user, no operation name for the rwb-access read, and no ID mapping for the two events
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md (RWB-AD-022); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S9 Partner management v2.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3.md; _work/msr/context/S9.md
section: s3 Preconditions, s7 AC3 and AC5, s11 Data, s12.2 REST operations consumed, s12.3 Events published, s12.7 Tables owned
description: Combined for this contract baseline: (a) partner_user is a table of S9 with no published element, no path and no account status list, and its fields appear only as DF-REF-212 to DF-REF-217 of the Logical Data Model, so the contract fixes it as a table; (b) the rwb-access contract dependency RWB-P4-E1022-CON of the app story has no published operation name and no document named in any extract, and this CON story has no contract dependency row of its own, so the consumed row carries a placeholder; (c) the ownership rows give the two event IDs EV-20 and EV-21 without their names and TSD S9 T5.3 gives the two names without their IDs, so the mapping is taken in the ownership order; (d) TSD S9 T-A.2 gives one message per error code for some conditions and none for others, so the message IDs per condition carry the FSD set.
evidence: TSD S9 T-A.1 and T-A.2 publish six operations and no user operation; context pack events list EV-20 and EV-21 only; TSD S9 T5.3 lists InstructionIssued and PartnerResultSubmitted without IDs; context pack ownership rows give 6 REST operations, 2 events and 1 workflow for S9.
owner_role: Solution architect; tech lead of rwb-partner
proposed: Publish a PartnerUser element or confirm the table-only reading, publish the rwb-access operation names, and map EV-20 and EV-21 to their names in the Event and Messaging Design.
